Is there a keyboard shortcut in Obsidian to search for a page? card

Short answer: Yes — Cmd+O (macOS) / Ctrl+O (Windows/Linux) opens the Quick Switcher, Obsidian's equivalent to Logseq's Cmd+K and Slack's Cmd+K. Type any part of a file name to jump to it; press Enter to open.

Is there a VSCode/Extension that helps obsidian users have an obsidian-compatible view of obsidian markdown files and navigate between wiki links?
“Obsidian-compatible” here means wiki-style [[links]], optional backlinks/embeds, and navigating notes on disk like a vault—not pixel-perfect Obsidian UI.

Is there a VSCode/Extension that helps obsidian users have an obsidian-compatible view of obsidian markdown files and navigate between wiki links?

Yes. Several VSCode/Extensions add Obsidian-like wikilinks, navigation (go to definition / Ctrl/Cmd+click), autocomplete on [[, and sometimes backlinks or embeds. None fully replicate Obsidian’s reading view, but many teams combine one of these with the built-in Markdown preview (VSCode/Command/Markdown/Open Preview / preview to the side).
Is there a VSCode/Extension that helps obsidian users have an obsidian-compatible view of obsidian markdown files and navigate between wiki links?
Is there a VSCode/Extension that helps obsidian users have an obsidian-compatible view of obsidian markdown files and navigate between wiki links?

Foam (repo) — Large install base; wikilink completion, go to definition, peek references, graph, daily notes, optional link reference definitions for standard Markdown compatibility, and navigation in the Markdown preview (per marketplace/docs). Good default if you want an Obsidian-adjacent workspace inside VS Code.
Markdown Notes (repo) — Longstanding [[wiki-links]], backlinks panel, peek/go to definition, autocomplete, piped links; explicitly aimed at Obsidian/Roam-style workflows.
WikiLens (repo) — Roam/Obsidian-like UX: page-centric explorer, backlinks, ![[embeds]], daily pages. Check repo activity if you care about ongoing maintenance.
Is there a VSCode/Extension that helps obsidian users have an obsidian-compatible view of obsidian markdown files and navigate between wiki links?
Obsidian Navigation — Click/hover to open linked .md files for [[FileName]] in the editor; marketplace notes Markdown preview pane link navigation is not implemented yet (planned).
obsidian-vscode-extension — Click wikilinks, create missing notes, [[ completion, hover shows linked file content (smaller extension by install count).

AS Notes — Wikilinks, backlinks, rename propagation; claims Markdown preview resolves nested wikilinks for navigation-style reading (verify in trial against your vault layout).

Vault layout matters: Obsidian often uses flat or folder notes with unique names; some extensions assume unique filenames vs path-relative wikilinks—match extension settings to how your vault is stored.
Preview vs editor: Built-in preview follows standard Markdown; wikilink clicking in preview is extension-dependent (Foam documents preview navigation; Obsidian Navigation explicitly does not yet).

Should a team vault in git commit its community plugins' code, or only the list of plugins?

Prompted by git status in a work team's knowledge garden on 2026-10-23: Obsidian had updated easy-copy, folder-notes and obsidian-git, so their tracked manifest.json files showed as modified and their main.js, styles.css and data.json showed as untracked.

Short answer: For a team vault that newcomers clone, commit each plugin's whole folder (manifest.json, main.js, styles.css) and decide data.json plugin by plugin. Committing only manifest.json records versions but installs nothing, so a fresh clone opens with plugins turned on that cannot load.

Obsidian does not download a plugin that community-plugins.json lists but .obsidian/plugins/<id>/ lacks. The older gardens' design says main.js and styles.css are files "that Obsidian re-downloads when plugins are installed". That holds only when someone installs the plugin by hand; nothing re-downloads them on clone.

When a vault arrives with plugin code present, Obsidian asks once whether to trust the author and turn on community plugins, or open the vault in restricted mode. See Plugin security. Restricted mode leaves the files on disk and ignores them.

Obsidian Git's Tips and Tricks gives three .gitignore choices: all of .obsidian/, only .obsidian/plugins (to keep plugin settings that may hold secrets out of git), or only workspace.json. It does not split main.js from manifest.json.
